files.summary: Validating chess SIMD name: validating-chess-simd description: Use when changing SIMD or floating-point NNUE code in a UCI chess engine, preparing an x86 Windows executable, or evaluating speed and Elo claims for such a candidate. Preserve arithmetic semantics before measuring speed. Establish playing strength with games under equal clocks. For the Forge reference, see [tested commands and limitations](../../../validation/nnue-avx2-9850x3d/README.md). The latest explicit user validation/retention contract takes precedence over this workflow; preserve older frozen evidence when applying a newer contract to a new run.

Validating chess strength name: validating-chess-strength description: Use when evaluating chess-engine Elo or Stockfish claims, planning Fastchess paired matches or SPRT, encountering timeouts or incomplete pairs, or comparing fixed-node search quality with equal-clock strength. A match establishes evidence only for its frozen opponent, resource limit and stopping rule. Correctness, speed, fixed-node search quality and equal-clock playing strength are separate results. Record source commits/diffs, original archive, network, compiler/flags, executable and runner SHA-256, runner version/source pin, settings, exact openings, seed, CPU allocation/affinity/cgroup and stopping rule. Preserve source-to-binary build provenance: a declared commit plus executable hash alone does not authenticate that relationship. Sections: Freeze before play

Reference skill application scenarios These are documentation tests, not games or strength evidence. No matches are launched by the tests. During preparation of the dedicated quality runner, the initial implementation used concurrency 2 for native SPRT. Source inspection then established that an accepted boundary sets `atomic::stop`, interrupting another in-flight game without finishing its opening pair. A retained first game can therefore become an orphan. The runner was corrected to serial SPRT before play. This is a concrete operational failure Sections: Baseline failure observed before this skill

Validating root search accounting name: validating-root-search-accounting description: Use when changing chess-search root effort counters, move-identity accounting, aspiration-retry statistics or effort-based time allocation, especially when root move ordering changes between iterations. Attribute work to stable move identities before interpreting its effect on stopping. Correct counters, offline timing arithmetic, observed timed stops and playing strength require separate evidence. 1. **Freeze the question.** Record parent/candidate source, network, compiler/flags, binaries, instrumentation patch and trace hashes. Read the current [status](../../../validation/root-effort-20261019/STATUS.md). Sections: Workflow

Scenarios and verification limits The archived actual 6.4.7 search has four-FEN untimed PV/score/node instrumentation parity. At middlegame depth 7, selected `c3d5`'s ordinal bucket contains 1355 nodes from 4 moves, while that move contributes 601 of 3355 local nodes. Offline effort factors are 1.146125 versus 1.370864. Metadata explicitly records `timed_stop_observed=false`; these are counter/arithmetic observations. At authoring, source `7125b337` implements the stable-identity candidate; candidate trace agreement and full GREEN remain pending. Hosted job `39325939081` concerns 6.4.7, not this 6.4.8 change. Read STATUS for later evidence. Sections: Recorded failing control

Validating shared chess TT name: validating-shared-chess-tt description: Use when investigating shared chess-engine transposition-table races, changing TT probe/store interfaces or replacement destinations, considering single-worker lock bypass, or validating search and TT lifecycle changes with ThreadSanitizer. Validate coherent entry access, search-policy preservation and storage lifetime separately. A race-free snapshot does not establish history-dependent score eligibility, faster search or stronger play. 1. **Recover actual source.** Inspect trees and patches; checkpoint documents or model results are not implementations. Record commits/diffs, callers, compiler/flags and binary provenance. Preserve rejected proposals and original failures. Sections: Practical workflow

Application scenarios and verification limits These are documentation checks, not new engine tests or match evidence. This is a conditional ownership protocol, not a general exemption from locking. Default public Shared/SMP calls retain coherent striped access. Only an explicit opt-in with exactly one search worker may acquire a coarse gate across recursive search; no helper may be launched or joined while that lease exists. Keep per-entry stripes scoped to individual operations or drain steps. The reviewed protocol acquires the coarse gate, release-stores `requested=true`, Sections: Bounded owner lease

Chess Engine Forge Chess Engine Forge 6.4.0 is a C++20 UCI chess engine. The 6.x series is a strength rewrite: the move generator, search, and evaluation were rebuilt from the ground up for playing strength, replacing the conservative 5.x search. 6.1.0 added multi-threaded search (`Threads`), tuning options and the NNUE training tools; 6.2.0 added a built-in engine-generated opening book with Polyglot support, cutoff-count LMR, material correction history, new evaluation terms with a retuned table, a faster move picker and prebuilt Zen 4

Trainer for Forge's NNUE evaluation. Public NNUE update microbenchmark `tools/nnue_update_benchmark.cpp` measures calls to the actual out-of-line `forge::nnue::update` in the linked frozen core. It contains no replacement arithmetic and does not train or change weights. This is a microkernel result, not engine NPS, playing strength, Windows performance, or physical Ryzen evidence. At authoring, no compilation or timing run was performed. The default invocation performs 2,000,000 timed updates from a deterministic corpus of real legal transitions, with up to 16,384 separate warmup calls.

NNUE update differential driver `tools/nnue_update_snapshot.cpp` calls the actual public NNUE API. Compile the same driver separately against an immutable pre-fusion core and the candidate core; compare their complete binary streams. It contains no copied update arithmetic and does not calculate an expected result with a second formula. At driver authoring, only static review was performed. Compilation and runtime validation are owned by the main experiment; this note claims no passing result. The driver is not added to CMake. Coverage:

Pawn-span-fill review invariants (before final stable-patch review). For an enemy pawn on file f/rank r, the old expression `passed_pawn_mask(color,square) & ~forward_file(color,square)` contains exactly adjacent valid files at every rank strictly forward of r. Immediate pawn attacks start those files one rank forward. Inclusive same-file forward fill must therefore reproduce that old mask, including empty spans at the terminal rank and one adjacent file at a/h edges. With unsigned 64-bit input, successive OR shifts by 8, 16 and 32 produce offsets 0 through 7 ranks. None changes a file; high bits fall off for White and low bits for Black. Every shift count is below 64. Select relevant tools automatically, without requiring the user to name them. Use the smallest sufficient set; do not run every connected plugin for the same question.

Improve GrokChess name: improve-grokchess description: Improve GrokChess and other UCI chess engines through source-grounded engineering. Use when asked to make GrokChess stronger, pursue Stockfish-level play, choose or implement search or NNUE improvements, continue experiments, or plan the next development cycle. Prioritize TypeScript/JavaScript GrokChess; adapt to Forge and other engines when requested. Turn an authorized improvement request into a tested code change and a recoverable experiment. Optimize playing strength at the intended wall-clock time. Treat beating full-strength Stockfish as a research goal whose achievement requires direct match evidence.

Forge and GrokChess Coordinator name: coordinate-chess-engines description: Use when coordinating Forge, GrokChess, or related UCI engine development across GitHub and experiments, continuing an improvement run, reviewing Sol's progress in couns0538-sketch/dwqww, or selecting skills and plugins for a source-grounded engine task. Resume Engine Development name: resume-engine-development description: Use when continuing Forge, GrokChess, Aurora, or another UCI engine from a saved branch, checkpoint, interrupted experiment, hourly cycle, or handoff, especially after stale reports, missing binaries, blocked publication, or repeated diagnostic-only cycles. Not for unrelated programming tasks. Turn a continuation request into progress on the unfinished engine experiment, with recoverable evidence. Use `improve-grokchess` and `validate-chess-engine` when available; use `optimize-grokchess-speed` for an exact-behavior speed contract.

Validate Chess Engine Improvements name: validate-chess-engine description: Validate GrokChess, Forge, and other UCI engines. Use when investigating illegal moves, state or TT bugs, checking perft or UCI behavior, comparing engine candidates, running fastchess SPRT, interpreting Elo/Stockfish claims, or deciding whether a search, evaluation, NNUE, or speed change is ready to accept. Return separate conclusions about correctness, speed, and playing strength. Choose the smallest evidence set that resolves the actual question, then complete the required gate. Keep original artifacts and make incomplete evidence explicit.

Native Experiment Integrity name: native-experiment-integrity description: Use when freezing, recovering, resuming, auditing, or accepting a native chess-engine experiment, especially fastchess SPRT, paired PGNs, interrupted concurrent matches, changed binaries or networks, missing checkpoints, or claimed Elo gains. Chess Engine Forge 5.31.0 -> 6.4.0: experiment record This document lists every measured experiment of the 6.x strength work (12-14 October 2026, four release rounds): what was tried, how it was measured, the exact result and whether it was adopted. Every match number below was re-read from the match directory's `console.txt` (last `Games:` line, and for SPRT runs the last `LLR`/`accepted` line) and from the game count of its `games.pgn`; the games themselves are in `all-match-pgns.zip` next to this file (index at the end). The `bench 11` signatures were re-run on the binaries that played the matches Sections: Baseline and releases

Release 6.0.0 strength validation Stockfish 19 (official `sf_19` release, `stockfish-linux-x86-64-universal`) with `UCI_LimitStrength=true`, `UCI_Elo=2800` (6.0.0 and 6.1.0 matches) or `UCI_Elo=3000` (6.2.0-6.4.0 matches), `Threads=1`, `Hash=64`. At these settings Stockfish chooses its move at a limited depth from a MultiPV-4 set with the skill-level randomisation (`Skill::pick_best`); its Elo scale is anchored to CCRL blitz ratings. Its playing strength is therefore essentially independent of the time control, while Forge's is not. Sections: Reference opponent

Forge 6.4.2 underpromotion candidate This candidate fixes a move-completeness error: ordinary main search obtained promotions through noisy generation, which emitted queens only, while its quiet stage excluded all promotions. Rook, bishop and knight promotions could therefore disappear from search unless already supplied by TT or check-evasion handling. Noisy generation now emits all four choices for either color, including captures. Evaluation, NNUE weights, SEE, TT policy and search tuning are unchanged from the clock/stalemate candidate.

files.summary: Validating chess SIMD name: validating-chess-simd description: Use when changing SIMD or floating-point NNUE code in a UCI chess engine, preparing an x86 Windows executable, or evaluating speed and Elo claims for such a candidate. Preserve arithmetic semantics before measuring speed. Establish playing strength with games under equal clocks. For the Forge reference, see [tested commands and limitations](../../../validation/nnue-avx2-9850x3d/README.md). 1. Record baseline commit, candidate commit/diff, network checksum, compiler version, complete build flags, executable checksums, target CPU and OS. Use existing isolated checkouts; create no worktree unless requested. Build an immutable baseline export and candidate in separate directories with identical compiler options. Never use the cloud CPU's `-march=native` for another person's computer. Sections: Reproducible reference procedure

Validating chess strength name: validating-chess-strength description: Use when evaluating chess-engine Elo or Stockfish claims, planning Fastchess paired matches or SPRT, encountering timeouts or incomplete pairs, or comparing fixed-node search quality with equal-clock strength. A match establishes evidence only for its frozen opponent, resource limit and stopping rule. Correctness, speed, fixed-node search quality and equal-clock playing strength are separate results. Record source commits/diffs, original archive, network, compiler/flags, executable and runner SHA-256, runner version/source pin, settings, exact openings, seed, CPU allocation/affinity/cgroup and stopping rule. Preserve source-to-binary build provenance: a declared commit plus executable hash alone does not authenticate that relationship. Sections: Freeze before play

Reference skill application scenarios These are documentation tests, not games or strength evidence. No matches are launched by the tests. During preparation of the dedicated quality runner, the initial implementation used concurrency 2 for native SPRT. Source inspection then established that an accepted boundary sets `atomic::stop`, interrupting another in-flight game without finishing its opening pair. A retained first game can therefore become an orphan. The runner was corrected to serial SPRT before play. This is a concrete operational failure Sections: Baseline failure observed before this skill

Validating root search accounting name: validating-root-search-accounting description: Use when changing chess-search root effort counters, move-identity accounting, aspiration-retry statistics or effort-based time allocation, especially when root move ordering changes between iterations. Attribute work to stable move identities before interpreting its effect on stopping. Correct counters, offline timing arithmetic, observed timed stops and playing strength require separate evidence. 1. **Freeze the question.** Record parent/candidate source, network, compiler/flags, binaries, instrumentation patch and trace hashes. Read the current [status](../../../validation/root-effort-20261019/STATUS.md). Sections: Workflow

Scenarios and verification limits The archived actual 6.4.7 search has four-FEN untimed PV/score/node instrumentation parity. At middlegame depth 7, selected `c3d5`'s ordinal bucket contains 1355 nodes from 4 moves, while that move contributes 601 of 3355 local nodes. Offline effort factors are 1.146125 versus 1.370864. Metadata explicitly records `timed_stop_observed=false`; these are counter/arithmetic observations. At authoring, source `7125b337` implements the stable-identity candidate; candidate trace agreement and full GREEN remain pending. Hosted job `39325939081` concerns 6.4.7, not this 6.4.8 change. Read STATUS for later evidence. Sections: Recorded failing control

Validating shared chess TT name: validating-shared-chess-tt description: Use when investigating shared chess-engine transposition-table races, changing TT probe/store interfaces or replacement destinations, considering single-worker lock bypass, or validating search and TT lifecycle changes with ThreadSanitizer. Validate coherent entry access, search-policy preservation and storage lifetime separately. A race-free snapshot does not establish history-dependent score eligibility, faster search or stronger play. 1. **Recover actual source.** Inspect trees and patches; checkpoint documents or model results are not implementations. Record commits/diffs, callers, compiler/flags and binary provenance. Preserve rejected proposals and original failures. Sections: Practical workflow

Application scenarios and verification limits These are documentation checks, not new engine tests or match evidence. This is a conditional ownership protocol, not a general exemption from locking. Default public Shared/SMP calls retain coherent striped access. Only an explicit opt-in with exactly one search worker may acquire a coarse gate across recursive search; no helper may be launched or joined while that lease exists. Keep per-entry stripes scoped to individual operations or drain steps. The reviewed protocol acquires the coarse gate, release-stores `requested=true`, Sections: Bounded owner lease

Trainer for Forge's NNUE evaluation. Public NNUE update microbenchmark `tools/nnue_update_benchmark.cpp` measures calls to the actual out-of-line `forge::nnue::update` in the linked frozen core. It contains no replacement arithmetic and does not train or change weights. This is a microkernel result, not engine NPS, playing strength, Windows performance, or physical Ryzen evidence. At authoring, no compilation or timing run was performed. The default invocation performs 2,000,000 timed updates from a deterministic corpus of real legal transitions, with up to 16,384 separate warmup calls.

NNUE update differential driver `tools/nnue_update_snapshot.cpp` calls the actual public NNUE API. Compile the same driver separately against an immutable pre-fusion core and the candidate core; compare their complete binary streams. It contains no copied update arithmetic and does not calculate an expected result with a second formula. At driver authoring, only static review was performed. Compilation and runtime validation are owned by the main experiment; this note claims no passing result. The driver is not added to CMake. Coverage:

Pawn-span-fill review invariants (before final stable-patch review). For an enemy pawn on file f/rank r, the old expression `passed_pawn_mask(color,square) & ~forward_file(color,square)` contains exactly adjacent valid files at every rank strictly forward of r. Immediate pawn attacks start those files one rank forward. Inclusive same-file forward fill must therefore reproduce that old mask, including empty spans at the terminal rank and one adjacent file at a/h edges. With unsigned 64-bit input, successive OR shifts by 8, 16 and 32 produce offsets 0 through 7 ranks. None changes a file; high bits fall off for White and low bits for Black. Every shift count is below 64. Select relevant tools automatically, without requiring the user to name them. Use the smallest sufficient set; do not run every connected plugin for the same question.

Improve GrokChess name: improve-grokchess description: Improve GrokChess and other UCI chess engines through source-grounded engineering. Use when asked to make GrokChess stronger, pursue Stockfish-level play, choose or implement search or NNUE improvements, continue experiments, or plan the next development cycle. Prioritize TypeScript/JavaScript GrokChess; adapt to Forge and other engines when requested. Turn an authorized improvement request into a tested code change and a recoverable experiment. Optimize playing strength at the intended wall-clock time. Treat beating full-strength Stockfish as a research goal whose achievement requires direct match evidence.

Forge and GrokChess Coordinator name: coordinate-chess-engines description: Use when coordinating Forge, GrokChess, or related UCI engine development across GitHub and experiments, continuing an improvement run, reviewing Sol's progress in couns0538-sketch/dwqww, or selecting skills and plugins for a source-grounded engine task. Resume Engine Development name: resume-engine-development description: Use when continuing Forge, GrokChess, Aurora, or another UCI engine from a saved branch, checkpoint, interrupted experiment, hourly cycle, or handoff, especially after stale reports, missing binaries, blocked publication, or repeated diagnostic-only cycles. Not for unrelated programming tasks. Turn a continuation request into progress on the unfinished engine experiment, with recoverable evidence. Use `improve-grokchess` and `validate-chess-engine` when available; use `optimize-grokchess-speed` for an exact-behavior speed contract.

Validate Chess Engine Improvements name: validate-chess-engine description: Validate GrokChess, Forge, and other UCI engines. Use when investigating illegal moves, state or TT bugs, checking perft or UCI behavior, comparing engine candidates, running fastchess SPRT, interpreting Elo/Stockfish claims, or deciding whether a search, evaluation, NNUE, or speed change is ready to accept. Return separate conclusions about correctness, speed, and playing strength. Choose the smallest evidence set that resolves the actual question, then complete the required gate. Keep original artifacts and make incomplete evidence explicit.

Native Experiment Integrity name: native-experiment-integrity description: Use when freezing, recovering, resuming, auditing, or accepting a native chess-engine experiment, especially fastchess SPRT, paired PGNs, interrupted concurrent matches, changed binaries or networks, missing checkpoints, or claimed Elo gains. Chess Engine Forge 5.31.0 -> 6.4.0: experiment record This document lists every measured experiment of the 6.x strength work (12-14 October 2026, four release rounds): what was tried, how it was measured, the exact result and whether it was adopted. Every match number below was re-read from the match directory's `console.txt` (last `Games:` line, and for SPRT runs the last `LLR`/`accepted` line) and from the game count of its `games.pgn`; the games themselves are in `all-match-pgns.zip` next to this file (index at the end). The `bench 11` signatures were re-run on the binaries that played the matches Sections: Baseline and releases

Release 6.0.0 strength validation Stockfish 19 (official `sf_19` release, `stockfish-linux-x86-64-universal`) with `UCI_LimitStrength=true`, `UCI_Elo=2800` (6.0.0 and 6.1.0 matches) or `UCI_Elo=3000` (6.2.0-6.4.0 matches), `Threads=1`, `Hash=64`. At these settings Stockfish chooses its move at a limited depth from a MultiPV-4 set with the skill-level randomisation (`Skill::pick_best`); its Elo scale is anchored to CCRL blitz ratings. Its playing strength is therefore essentially independent of the time control, while Forge's is not. Sections: Reference opponent

S-IT idea sources - **FIDE Laws of Chess, Article 9.2** (handbook.fide.com, chapter E012023). The game is drawn upon a correct claim by a player having the move when the same position, for at least the third time: - 9.2.1 is about to appear: the player writes the move on the scoresheet (it cannot be changed) and declares the intention to make it; - 9.2.2 has just appeared. - 9.2.3: positions are the same when the same player has the move, the same pieces occupy the same squares, and the possible moves are the same. En passant and castling rights that differ make the positions different.

S-IT: intended-threefold claim (FIDE 9.2.1), UCI `IntendedThreefold` (default false) `setoption name IntendedThreefold value true`: at every non-root search node and every quiescence node, the side to move may claim a draw when one of its legal moves would create the third occurrence of a position (FIDE 9.2.1). That right is a floor at the draw score (0): - `beta <= 0`: the node returns 0 (fail high on the claim alone). - Otherwise alpha is raised to 0 and the node's value is `max(search value, 0)`, so a mate still beats the optional draw (mate precedence). Forge offline SPSA tuner (`tools/spsa`, R3-4) Tunes integer UCI spin options of Forge with SPSA: every iteration plays a short fastchess mini-match between theta+ = theta + c_k·Δ and theta- = theta - c_k·Δ (Δ = ±1 per parameter), then moves theta along the measured score difference. Offline means the tuner is a single Python process that drives fastchess on one machine; it is resumable at any iteration boundary. Python 3.10+, standard library only. fastchess only sends `setoption` for options an engine advertises (with `-strict` it stops on the warning), and Sections: The engine side: 20 advertised search constants

Unified portable archive namespace regression The prior packager treated file names and directory names separately. A directory A/child.txt and a file a could both be archived successfully, although their destination paths collide on Windows. Distinct A and a directories, and case aliases of implicit ancestors across separate mappings, were also accepted. Tests were added before the fix. red.stderr records three concrete failures across 23 tests: file/directory collision, two explicit case-alias directories, and differently capitalized implicit parents. Same-spelling shared implicit parents and already-rejected file-ancestor mappings were checked at the same time. The old packager and that first test revision are preserved.

Public NNUE update microbenchmark `tools/nnue_update_benchmark.cpp` measures calls to the actual out-of-line `forge::nnue::update` in the linked frozen core. It contains no replacement arithmetic and does not train or change weights. This is a microkernel result, not engine NPS, playing strength, Windows performance, or physical Ryzen evidence. At authoring, no compilation or timing run was performed. The default invocation performs 2,000,000 timed updates from a deterministic corpus of real legal transitions, with up to 16,384 separate warmup calls.

NNUE update differential driver `tools/nnue_update_snapshot.cpp` calls the actual public NNUE API. Compile the same driver separately against an immutable pre-fusion core and the candidate core; compare their complete binary streams. It contains no copied update arithmetic and does not calculate an expected result with a second formula. At driver authoring, only static review was performed. Compilation and runtime validation are owned by the main experiment; this note claims no passing result. The driver is not added to CMake. Coverage:

With unsigned 64-bit input, successive OR shifts by 8, 16 and 32 produce offsets 0 through 7 ranks. None changes a file; high bits fall off for White and low bits for Black. Trainer for Forge's NNUE evaluation. S-IT idea sources - **FIDE Laws of Chess, Article 9.2** (handbook.fide.com, chapter E012023). The game is drawn upon a correct claim by a player having the move when the same position, for at least the third time: - 9.2.1 is about to appear: the player writes the move on the scoresheet (it cannot be changed) and declares the intention to make it; - 9.2.2 has just appeared. - 9.2.3: positions are the same when the same player has the move, the same pieces occupy the same squares, and the possible moves are the same. En passant and castling rights that differ make the positions different.

S-IT: intended-threefold claim (FIDE 9.2.1), UCI `IntendedThreefold` (default false) `setoption name IntendedThreefold value true`: at every non-root search node and every quiescence node, the side to move may claim a draw when one of its legal moves would create the third occurrence of a position (FIDE 9.2.1). Forge offline SPSA tuner (`tools/spsa`, R3-4) Tunes integer UCI spin options of Forge with SPSA: every iteration plays a short fastchess mini-match between theta+ = theta + c_k·Δ and theta- = theta - c_k·Δ (Δ = ±1 per parameter), then moves theta along the measured score difference. Offline means the tuner is a single Python process that drives fastchess on one machine; it is resumable at any iteration boundary. Python 3.10+, standard library only. fastchess only sends `setoption` for options an engine advertises (with `-strict` it stops on the warning), and Sections: The engine side: 20 advertised search constants

name | fen | moves Forced perpetual-check draws. The side to move is a rook and pawns behind (it loses without the checks), and every reply of the opponent to its queen checks is a forced king move (no other square, no interposition, no capture), so the game is a draw by repetition. Q1/Q2 are two geometries, Q3/Q4 their colour mirrors, Q5/Q6 file mirrors. S-IT idea sources - **FIDE Laws of Chess, Article 9.2** (handbook.fide.com, chapter E012023). The game is drawn upon a correct claim by a player having the move when the same position, for at least the third time: - 9.2.1 is about to appear: the player writes the move on the scoresheet (it cannot be changed) and declares the intention to make it; - 9.2.2 has just appeared. - 9.2.3: positions are the same when the same player has the move, the same pieces occupy the same squares, and the possible moves are the same. En passant and castling rights that differ make the positions different.

Forge offline SPSA tuner (`tools/spsa`, R3-4) Tunes integer UCI spin options of Forge with SPSA: every iteration plays a short fastchess mini-match between theta+ = theta + c_k·Δ and theta- = theta - c_k·Δ (Δ = ±1 per parameter), then moves theta along the measured score difference. Offline means the tuner is a single Python process that drives fastchess on one machine; it is resumable at any iteration boundary. Python 3.10+, standard library only. fastchess only sends `setoption` for options an engine advertises (with `-strict` it stops on the warning), and Sections: The engine side: 20 advertised search constants

S-IT idea sources - **FIDE Laws of Chess, Article 9.2** (handbook.fide.com, chapter E012023). The game is drawn upon a correct claim by a player having the move when the same position, for at least the third time: - 9.2.1 is about to appear: the player writes the move on the scoresheet (it cannot be changed) and declares the intention to make it; - 9.2.2 has just appeared. - 9.2.3: positions are the same when the same player has the move, the same pieces occupy the same squares, and the possible moves are the same. En passant and castling rights that differ make the positions different.

S-IT: intended-threefold claim (FIDE 9.2.1), UCI `IntendedThreefold` (default false) `setoption name IntendedThreefold value true`: at every non-root search node and every quiescence node, the side to move may claim a draw when one of its legal moves would create the third occurrence of a position (FIDE 9.2.1). Forge offline SPSA tuner (`tools/spsa`, R3-4) Tunes integer UCI spin options of Forge with SPSA: every iteration plays a short fastchess mini-match between theta+ = theta + c_k·Δ and theta- = theta - c_k·Δ (Δ = ±1 per parameter), then moves theta along the measured score difference. Offline means the tuner is a single Python process that drives fastchess on one machine; it is resumable at any iteration boundary. S-IT idea sources - **FIDE Laws of Chess, Article 9.2** (handbook.fide.com, chapter E012023). The game is drawn upon a correct claim by a player having the move when the same position, for at least the third time: - 9.2.1 is about to appear: the player writes the move on the scoresheet (it cannot be changed) and declares the intention to make it; - 9.2.2 has just appeared. - 9.2.3: positions are the same when the same player has the move, the same pieces occupy the same squares, and the possible moves are the same. En passant and castling rights that differ make the positions different.

S-IT: intended-threefold claim (FIDE 9.2.1), UCI `IntendedThreefold` (default false) `setoption name IntendedThreefold value true`: at every non-root search node and every quiescence node, the side to move may claim a draw when one of its legal moves would create the third occurrence of a position (FIDE 9.2.1). That right is a floor at the draw score (0): - `beta <= 0`: the node returns 0 (fail high on the claim alone). - Otherwise alpha is raised to 0 and the node's value is `max(search value, 0)`, so a mate still beats the optional draw (mate precedence). S-IT idea sources - **FIDE Laws of Chess, Article 9.2** (handbook.fide.com, chapter E012023). The game is drawn upon a correct claim by a player having the move when the same position, for at least the third time: - 9.2.1 is about to appear: the player writes the move on the scoresheet (it cannot be changed) and declares the intention to make it; - 9.2.2 has just appeared. - 9.2.3: positions are the same when the same player has the move, the same pieces occupy the same squares, and the possible moves are the same. En passant and castling rights that differ make the positions different.

S-IT: intended-threefold claim (FIDE 9.2.1), UCI `IntendedThreefold` (default false) `setoption name IntendedThreefold value true`: at every non-root search node and every quiescence node, the side to move may claim a draw when one of its legal moves would create the third occurrence of a position (FIDE 9.2.1). Chess Engine Forge Chess Engine Forge 6.4.0 is a C++20 UCI chess engine. The 6.x series is a strength rewrite: the move generator, search, and evaluation were rebuilt from the ground up for playing strength, replacing the conservative 5.x search. 6.1.0 added multi-threaded search (`Threads`), tuning options and the NNUE training tools; 6.2.0 added a built-in engine-generated opening book with Polyglot support, cutoff-count LMR, material correction history, new evaluation terms with a retuned table, a faster move picker and prebuilt Zen 4

Release state — Chess Engine Forge 6.4.0 Status: **strength release; first shipped neural network (residual NNUE, +86 Elo at fixed nodes and +45 Elo at 10+0.1 over 6.3.0), validated against Stockfish 19 at UCI_Elo 3000**. Against Stockfish 19 with `UCI_LimitStrength=true UCI_Elo=3000` (one thread, Hash 64, 8moves_v3 openings) the shipped binary scored 52.5 % over 100 games at 20+0.2 (35W 30L 35D, +17 +/- 53 Elo); 6.3.0 scored 50.0 % (33W 33L 34D) and 6.2.0 51.5 % (35W 32L 33D) under the same conditions, differences inside the noise of 100 games. One position (Forge-2, `rn1qkb1r/p1p1ppp1/1p1pbn2/7p/3P4/2N1PN2/PPP1BPPP/R1BQK2R w KQkq - 0 1`) showed 3/3 discrepant boundary scores: baseline 52/53/54, no-LMR 53/54/55 around depth-8 center +54. Release 6.0.0 strength validation Stockfish 19 (official `sf_19` release, `stockfish-linux-x86-64-universal`) with `UCI_LimitStrength=true`, `UCI_Elo=2800` (6.0.0 and 6.1.0 matches) or `UCI_Elo=3000` (6.2.0-6.4.0 matches), `Threads=1`, `Hash=64`. At these settings Stockfish chooses its move at a limited depth from a MultiPV-4 set with the skill-level randomisation (`Skill::pick_best`); its Elo scale is anchored to CCRL blitz ratings. Its playing strength is therefore essentially independent of the time control, while Forge's is not. Sections: Reference opponent

Chess Engine Forge Chess Engine Forge 6.4.0 is a C++20 UCI chess engine. The 6.x series is a strength rewrite: the move generator, search, and evaluation were rebuilt from the ground up for playing strength, replacing the conservative 5.x search. 6.1.0 added multi-threaded search (`Threads`), tuning options and the NNUE training tools; 6.2.0 added a built-in engine-generated opening book with Polyglot support, cutoff-count LMR, material correction history, new evaluation terms with a retuned table, a faster move picker and prebuilt Zen 4

Forge improvement log — 5.31.0, 2026-10-09 Validated immediate source: 5.30.0 SHA-256 `fd2f0d249b78bc353bc3a439464be0c4aec7a01eb1664f2c923f985aef74d0d7`. Current run examined 10 deterministic MIT Forge corpus positions at interior depth 9 with three score-boundary windows each, comparing the exact frozen baseline against an isolated no-LMR reference. One position (Forge-2, `rn1qkb1r/p1p1ppp1/1p1pbn2/7p/3P4/2N1PN2/PPP1BPPP/R1BQK2R w KQkq - 0 1`) showed 3/3 discrepant boundary scores: baseline 52/53/54, no-LMR 53/54/55 around depth-8 center +54. An independent full-window probe returned depth-9 +57 with baseline LMR and +62 without LMR. The proved problem is an LMR-dependent false fail-low relative to full-depth boundary search, not a measured gameplay loss. Two new baseline-failing regression assertions and adjacent board-state check establish the fix.

Trainer for Forge's NNUE evaluation. Architecture (per side-to-move perspective): 768 piece-square inputs -> Hidden accumulator, SCReLU activation, then a single output over both perspectives (2 * Hidden -> 1). Trained with Adam on the squared error between sigmoid(output) and a blend of game result and search score, using the same "<fen> <result> <score>" files that forge_texel consumes. Current run examined 10 deterministic MIT Forge corpus positions at interior depth 9 with three score-boundary windows each, comparing the exact frozen baseline against an isolated no-LMR reference. An independent full-window probe returned depth-9 +57 with baseline LMR and +62 without LMR. The proved problem is an LMR-dependent false fail-low relative to full-depth boundary search, not a measured gameplay loss. Two new baseline-failing regression assertions and adjacent board-state check establish the fix.

Chess Engine Forge 5.31.0 -> 6.4.0: experiment record This document lists every measured experiment of the 6.x strength work (12-14 October 2026, four release rounds): what was tried, how it was measured, the exact result and whether it was adopted. Every match number below was re-read from the match directory's `console.txt` (last `Games:` line, and for SPRT runs the last `LLR`/`accepted` line) and from the game count of its `games.pgn`; the games themselves are in `all-match-pgns.zip` next to this file (index at the end). The `bench 11` signatures were re-run on the binaries that played the matches Sections: Baseline and releases

Release 6.0.0 strength validation Stockfish 19 (official `sf_19` release, `stockfish-linux-x86-64-universal`) with `UCI_LimitStrength=true`, `UCI_Elo=2800` (6.0.0 and 6.1.0 matches) or `UCI_Elo=3000` (6.2.0-6.4.0 matches), `Threads=1`, `Hash=64`. At these settings Stockfish chooses its move at a limited depth from a MultiPV-4 set with the skill-level randomisation (`Skill::pick_best`); its Elo scale is anchored to CCRL blitz ratings. Its playing strength is therefore essentially independent of the time control, while Forge's is not. Sections: Reference opponent

Chess Engine Forge Chess Engine Forge 6.4.0 is a C++20 UCI chess engine. The 6.x series is a strength rewrite: the move generator, search, and evaluation were rebuilt from the ground up for playing strength, replacing the conservative 5.x search. 6.1.0 added multi-threaded search (`Threads`), tuning options and the NNUE training tools; 6.2.0 added a built-in engine-generated opening book with Polyglot support, cutoff-count LMR, material correction history, new evaluation terms with a retuned table, a faster move picker and prebuilt Zen 4

Release state — Chess Engine Forge 6.4.0 Status: **strength release; first shipped neural network (residual NNUE, +86 Elo at fixed nodes and +45 Elo at 10+0.1 over 6.3.0), validated against Stockfish 19 at UCI_Elo 3000**. Against Stockfish 19 with `UCI_LimitStrength=true UCI_Elo=3000` (one thread, Hash 64, 8moves_v3 openings) the shipped binary scored 52.5 % over 100 games at 20+0.2 (35W 30L 35D, +17 +/- 53 Elo); 6.3.0 scored 50.0 % (33W 33L 34D) and 6.2.0 51.5 % (35W 32L 33D) under the same conditions, differences inside the noise of 100 games. Match records live in `validation/release-6.0.0/`.

Forge improvement log — 5.31.0, 2026-10-09 Validated immediate source: 5.30.0 SHA-256 `fd2f0d249b78bc353bc3a439464be0c4aec7a01eb1664f2c923f985aef74d0d7`. Current run examined 10 deterministic MIT Forge corpus positions at interior depth 9 with three score-boundary windows each, comparing the exact frozen baseline against an isolated no-LMR reference. One position (Forge-2, `rn1qkb1r/p1p1ppp1/1p1pbn2/7p/3P4/2N1PN2/PPP1BPPP/R1BQK2R w KQkq - 0 1`) showed 3/3 discrepant boundary scores: baseline 52/53/54, no-LMR 53/54/55 around depth-8 center +54. An independent full-window probe returned depth-9 +57 with baseline LMR and +62 without LMR. The proved problem is an LMR-dependent false fail-low relative to full-depth boundary search, not a measured gameplay loss. Two new baseline-failing regression assertions and adjacent board-state check establish the fix.

Chess Engine Forge 5.31.0 -> 6.4.0: experiment record This document lists every measured experiment of the 6.x strength work (12-14 October 2026, four release rounds): what was tried, how it was measured, the exact result and whether it was adopted. Every match number below was re-read from the match directory's `console.txt` (last `Games:` line, and for SPRT runs the last `LLR`/`accepted` line) and from the game count of its `games.pgn`; the games themselves are in `all-match-pgns.zip` next to this file (index at the end). The `bench 11` signatures were re-run on the binaries that played the matches Sections: Baseline and releases

Release 6.0.0 strength validation Stockfish 19 (official `sf_19` release, `stockfish-linux-x86-64-universal`) with `UCI_LimitStrength=true`, `UCI_Elo=2800` (6.0.0 and 6.1.0 matches) or `UCI_Elo=3000` (6.2.0-6.4.0 matches), `Threads=1`, `Hash=64`. At these settings Stockfish chooses its move at a limited depth from a MultiPV-4 set with the skill-level randomisation (`Skill::pick_best`); its Elo scale is anchored to CCRL blitz ratings. Its playing strength is therefore essentially independent of the time control, while Forge's is not. Sections: Reference opponent

Forge time-management audit Audited the combo29 UCI clock on commit `16833ecc` (`lock/combo29-20261110`). Four defects were confirmed on a release build and fixed. The soft and hard allocation formulas were left as they are. `go` reads only the side to move. `wtime`/`btime` and `winc`/`binc` for the other side are ignored. `moves_to_go == 0` is sudden death. The default move overhead is 10 ms; the tests set it to 0 except for the overhead case. In `Worker::search`: - `movetime` wins over the clock. The hard limit is `max(1, movetime - overhead)`.
